regime: Risk-Off Trend Day (Selloff Extends, Gold Sold Hardest, Vol Rising)
summary: Risk-off did not stop at Thursday's close. The Nasdaq fell another 2.30 percent to 28,545.75 and the S&P lost 1.24 percent to 7,614.50, and both stayed pinned under their trend stops all session. December gold took the worst of it, down 3.69 percent to 3,884.40, slicing clean through the 4,000 round. Gold is not acting like a hedge here. It fell with everything else, which keeps pointing at broad cash-raising rather than a rotation. Crude was the only board that did not fall, up a few cents to 102.97, but it gave back a run to 104.98 and is barely holding its stop. VIX jumped about 13 percent to 19.4, so fear is still bid.

setups.entry: Trend-follow each instrument with its ATR stop.
setups.stop: Short while below: MNQ 28,685, MES 7,630, gold 3,930. Crude is above its 102.80 stop, so no short there yet.

setups.bias: MNQ, MES and December gold all closed below their ATR stops and EMA50 on a third straight trend-down day, so the trend-short is on. Crude is the lone long, above its stop by a hair.

setups.name: AVWAP Hand-off
setups.entry: Short the hand-off after an opening-range down break retests and fails AVWAP or NYVWAP.
setups.stop: Back above NYVWAP 28,550 or the OR high 28,809 invalidates.
setups.bias: MNQ broke the opening range down at 14:21 UTC and closed below it and below NYVWAP, the clean short-only hand-off. HOF is eligible Monday.

setups.name: AVWAP Bounce
setups.entry: Short rallies that fail at AVWAP or NYVWAP while price is below the stop.
setups.stop: A full reclaim of AVWAP 28,539 and the 28,685 stop invalidates.
setups.bias: Borderline. Price is below its stop and using AVWAP and NYVWAP as resistance, the continuation read, but a fast tape makes the retest timing tricky.

event.name: No scheduled US release (federal data subject to shutdown-related delays)
event.consensus: The federal data calendar stays thin and unreliable under the shutdown backdrop, so scheduled releases were not the driver.
event.actual: A third straight risk-off session. The post-FOMC unwind rolled into broad multi-day de-risking, with equities, gold and eventually crude's highs all under pressure.
event.surprise: Gold fell the hardest of all, down 3.69 percent, which reads as cash-raising rather than a safe-haven bid. VIX pushed toward 19.4.
event.nqReaction: NQ fell 2.30 percent, broke its opening range down at 14:21 UTC, stayed below its ATR stop and EMA50, and closed 28,545.75 after a 28,232.25 low.
event.crossAsset: MES minus 1.24 percent at 7,614.50. December gold minus 3.69 percent at 3,884.40, the worst board. December crude plus 0.10 percent at 102.97, green but faded from 104.98. VIX about 19.4, up roughly 13 percent.

observe.note: No OBSERVE-lane signals today. GAP_NQ and TSMOM252LO_NQ sit outside the Net Alpha Pro curriculum and are tracked for research only.

risk.sizing: Defensive. Three straight trend-down days with stops broken, so no new longs and reduced size overall.
risk.openRisk: MNQ, MES and gold are all below their ATR stops and EMA50, so the only trend intact is crude to the upside and it is holding by a hair. A multi-day break can keep extending, so treat bounces as suspect until a stop is reclaimed.
risk.note: Throttle state DEFENSIVE. No drawdown flags and the daily loss budget is unused, but the selloff is now three sessions deep: NQ lost another 2.30 percent, MES another 1.24 percent, and December gold fell the hardest at 3.69 percent, all closing below their ATR stops and EMA50. No new longs here. The long-only momentum edge (E3v2) is blocked with price below EMA50 and ROC negative. TSMOM can work the short side while price stays below the stops (MNQ 28,685, MES 7,630, gold 3,930), but keep size small into a fast tape with VIX near 19.4. Crude is the lone long, above its 102.80 stop by a hair after fading from 104.98, so treat it as the weakest long. The data calendar stays thin under the shutdown, so treat any headline as the catalyst. Daylight saving ends Nov 1; next policy event is the December FOMC.

psychology: Three sessions down in a row, and every bounce has been sold. The hard part of a trend like this is not spotting it, it is sitting still while it runs. Each new low looks like the bottom, and buying it has lost money three days running. The stops are falling and price keeps closing below them, so the market has not told you it is done. Wait for a reclaim before you trust any bounce. Patience is the position here, not prediction.

fullReport.title: NY Opening Range / HTA OPEN (MNQ)
fullReport.html:
Trend-down break that held. OR High 28,808.75, OR Low 28,668.25, Width 140.5 pts.

Anchored at the 13:30 UTC NY cash open. Price poked above the range at 13:57 UTC to 28,841.75 (a failed up-break), then broke down at 14:21 UTC at 28,628.5 and stayed under the range. The 20:00 house bar closed 28,545.75, below the opening range and just below NYVWAP 28,549.53. It is Friday with no FOMC or CPI, so all four HTA OPEN playbooks are eligible: BIR, HOF, MID and BNC. The clean short-only hand-off set up on the down break; there was no back-into-range because the close finished below the range. Volume is disclaimed on the continuous contract, so VWAP uses a typical-price mean.

Price rode the lower bands down intraday to a 28,232.25 low near the minus 3 sigma band, then recovered to close 28,545.75, right at the session mean. Because the close sits back at AVWAP rather than stretched beyond a band, the reversion edge is not in habitat today. A reversion-grade signal would need a stretched touch of the minus 2 or minus 3 sigma band followed by a reclaim, which did not hold into the close.
